---
title: "Smart greenhouses"
---

In this module, we will take a break from sequencing data, R, deep learning, and will talk about how simple programming and sensors can help agricultural practice. We will use a small microcontroller, simple sensors and make them communicate with each other using MakeCode. 

Here is what we will do in this module: 

## Lecture and quiz

When we meet in class I expect you to have listened to the module lecture below, and to have answered the discussion quiz on Canvas. 

[Greenhouse lecture](greenhouse_lecture.qmd){target="_blank"}. The recording is in Canvas.

Download the [PDF](greenhouse_lecture.pdf){download="greenhouse_lecture.pdf"} of the slides here.


### Learning outcomes.

After this module you can:

- explain what a microcontroller is and describe the sense → decide → act pattern
- tell digital, analog and serial signals apart
- connect a sensor to the micro:bit (G to G, V to V, S to S) and read its value in MakeCode
- use events, the `forever` loop, variables and `if / else` to make a device react to a sensor
- calibrate a sensor and describe at least one limitation you observed


## Discussion

In class, we will talk about these questions. Think about them before you come.

1. A greenhouse grower already checks the plants every morning. What could a sensor add, and what would it miss that the grower notices?
2. The DHT11 measures temperature to ±2 °C. For which greenhouse decisions is that good enough, and for which is it not?
3. Why can the micro:bit react to a button press with an event, but has to keep checking (polling) an external sensor?
4. Sensors in greenhouses and fields produce data over months. What would you need to record so that someone else can still use that data later?

## Exercises

You work in teams of 4–5 with one kit per team.

1. [Setup and exercises](exercises.qmd). Make notes on the exercises, the lab quiz will ask for thresholds and limitations you are noticing. 
2. [The kit: sensors and actuators](kit.qmd), to look up a component
3. Check [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd), for common problems if something does not work
